Real face photographs used as image fixtures for the biometric engine.

  same-person-a.png   <- opencv/opencv @ 4.x  samples/data/basketball1.png
  same-person-b.png   <- opencv/opencv @ 4.x  samples/data/basketball2.png
  other-person.png    <- opencv/opencv @ 4.x  samples/data/messi5.jpg

Source: https://github.com/opencv/opencv/tree/4.x/samples/data
Licence: Apache-2.0, the licence of the opencv/opencv repository. The
upstream licence text is at
https://github.com/opencv/opencv/blob/4.x/LICENSE.

These are published sample photographs, used here only as *pixels*:

  - No file in this directory is enrolled, and nothing in the application or the
    seed ever reads this directory. The test that uses them computes a
    descriptor and throws it away.
  - No embedding derived from them is stored, transmitted, or committed. The
    product's own rule is that biometric vectors never leave the backend and
    are never written to a fixture.
  - The photographs are of real, identifiable people. That is unavoidable for
    testing a face recognizer - a synthetic drawing is not a face, and YuNet
    correctly refuses to find one - so the images are used with their licence
    intact and kept out of every product code path.

same-person-a and same-person-b are two different photographs of the same
person, which is what makes them useful: the pair is what separates "this
engine measures identity" from "this engine measures a photograph". The engine's
measured similarity on them, and the cross-identity figure, are asserted in
tests/test_real_engine.py and recorded in docs/MODEL_EVALUATION.md.

What these three files are NOT: an accuracy evaluation. Three photographs of
two people cannot support a false-match rate, and no threshold in this project
is derived from them. Per-condition FAR/FRR measurement is Phase 10's work and
lives in docs/MODEL_EVALUATION.md.
